I farm 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will keep the full 10.1 mu in both winter wheat and summer maize. I am 62 and my household labor is limited, with some family members working off-farm, so I will choose a steady, familiar way of farming that does not depend on too much hand labor or risky changes. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield at the key stages, but I will still keep inputs moderate because I want stable returns and manageable costs. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, apply enough nitrogen for steady tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus for rooting, keep potassium modest, irrigate at the important times, and do a couple of pesticide sprays if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, keep fertilizer balanced but not excessive, irrigate when the crop is under the most stress, and manage pests with a couple of applications. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my equipment, my habits, and the need to turn fields around quickly between wheat and maize.
